title: The Jenkins Orphan Band marching through Savannah
summary: Kids followed the Charleston orphanage band, which played jazz with dance steps; Jabbo Smith and trombonist John Nick played in it. Willard asks whether Cat Anderson was in it.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: First paid gigs: pay, bands and young beginnings

blocks.x: And I watched quite a few fellows, and then I had an opportunity down there to watch a marching band but they played jazz from Charleston, South Carolina, which is only about 100 or so miles from Savannah. And this was the Jenkins Orphan Band. And before I left in 1926, why this band would come there. And he had some good musicians in there.

And we would follow them. Kids -- we would just follow them all down the streets, you know, because they reminded me a lot of that band that you see today from Grambling University because they did dance steps and they played jazz and they marched down the streets.
Was that the same band that Cat Anderson played in at one time? I know he was in some orphans --

Well, this was before Cat's time, you know, this was. But Jabbo Smith played in this orchestra, the trumpet player, and also there was a trombone player played in that orchestra named John Nick, N-i-c-k. And he was a fantastic trombone player. I never knew what happened to him
in later years, but he could play very good. And I would follow that band as a kid all down the street. I think I'm a little older than Cat, so this would have been a little --
-- Cat's time, yeah. Well, I'm a little older, yeah. I'll put it that way. But Cat might have played in one of those bands, but I didn't know him when he --
I wasn't sure about which -- the name of it, whether it was Jenkins or another one.
Well, Jenkins was from Charleston, South Carolina. I don't know where Cat was from originally.
